after: For any translated sample vector $v\in U$, telescope $v=(v-v_N[v])+\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}(v_{j+1}[v]-v_j[v])$, since $v_1[v]=0$. The absolute residual sign sum is at most $\lVert(\varepsilon_i)_i\rVert_2\lVert v-v_N[v]\rVert_2\le\sqrt n\epsilon_N$ by [F8]. For each $j<N$, use only the paired-center difference set $D_j:=\{v_{j+1}[v]-v_j[v]:v\in U\}$. It is a nonempty subset of $V_{j+1}-V_j$, so its cardinality is at most $|V_{j+1}||V_j|\le N_F(\mathcal G|S,\epsilon_{j+1})^2$, because covering numbers are nonincreasing with radius. Each paired difference has norm at most $\lVert v_{j+1}[v]-v\rVert_2+\lVert v-v_j[v]\rVert_2\le\epsilon_{j+1}+\epsilon_j=3\epsilon_{j+1}$. Step 2.1 applied to $D_j$ therefore bounds its expected maximum sign sum by $6\epsilon_{j+1}\sqrt{\log N_F(\mathcal G|S,\epsilon_{j+1})}$. Taking the supremum in the telescoping identity, summing these bounds, and dividing by $n$ gives $\widehat{\mathfrak R}_S(\mathcal G)\le\epsilon_N/\sqrt n+(6/n)\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}\epsilon_{j+1}\sqrt{\log N_F(\mathcal G|S,\epsilon_{j+1})}$.
